facts.fact: Blender 5.0 was released on November 18, 2025 (per search-result summary of the official release pages; the exact date line was in the search snippet, not re-verified on the page).

Blender 5.0.1 corrective release includes a fix to unbreak the Python 3.14 build, suggesting Python 3.14 was a build target for 5.0.x; the search did not confirm which Python version is bundled with 5.0.
A Blender 5.0.1 fix made a driver-evaluation test pass with Python newer than 3.11 (snippet-level evidence only).

Blender 5.0 added native buffer protocol support for mathutils types; Vector's underlying element type is now float32 rather than float64, and the buffer is exposed as non-contiguous, so scripts passing matrices/vectors to NumPy may need updating (the search summary did not clearly tie this to a specific page; treat as the Python API release-notes page's content, to be verified).
Blender 5.2 LTS was released July 14, 2026 and is supported until July 2028.
Blender 4.5 LTS remains supported until July 2027 (per search-result summary).
Blender's 2026 release plan named Blender 5.1 (March 2026), Blender 5.2 LTS (July 2026) and Blender 5.3 (November 2026).

CONFLICT on latest stable as of Nov 2026: the developer docs listing gives Blender 5.3 as current stable (November 10, 2026); the official download page lists 5.2.4 LTS dated November 10, 2026. Both are in the search summary; neither was opened directly.
CONFLICT on 5.2.4 date: the Blender Projects 5.2 LTS milestone shows 5.2.4 planned for November 16, 2026 in one view and November 17, 2026 in another.

contradictions: Latest stable version in November 2026: developer docs index says Blender 5.3 (Nov 10, 2026) while the official download page says 5.2.4 LTS (Nov 10, 2026). Not resolved; needs direct check on blender.org.
5.2.4 planned date: Nov 16, 2026 vs Nov 17, 2026 across two views of the same Blender Projects milestone (milestone/33).
